questions.stem: In what year was the PENG block first described?
In the PENG block, which structure lies in front of the injection plane?
For which surgery was the PENG block originally developed for postoperative analgesia?
Compared with femoral or fascia iliaca blocks, what does the PENG block aim to be for hip pain?
Which nerve supplying the anterior hip capsule is present only in some patients?
Which nerve mainly supplies the posterior hip capsule?
Why is the anterior hip capsule the target of the PENG block?
questions.answer: It carries most of the joint's sensory supply and most postoperative hip pain

questions.stem: Which three nerves' articular branches to the hip capsule does the PENG block cover?
questions.answer: Femoral, obturator and accessory obturator nerves

questions.stem: Down to which level does the PENG block cover proximal hip fractures?
What provides intertrochanteric cover with the PENG block?
options: Direct injection into the femoral head

questions.stem: What volume is described for achieving intertrochanteric cover with the PENG block?
Which cutaneous nerve is not blocked by the PENG block?
After which surgery is the PENG block indicated for postoperative analgesia?
For pain from which fractures is the PENG block indicated?
options: Proximal femur or femoral head fractures

questions.stem: What position is the patient in for the PENG block?
Where is the linear probe placed transversely for the PENG block?
options: Over the posterior superior iliac spine
Over the anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)

questions.stem: In the PENG block, how is the probe rotated to line up with the pubic ramus?
options: About 90 degrees, perpendicular to the inguinal crease
About 15 degrees, parallel to the inguinal crease
Rotate about 45 degrees, parallel to the inguinal crease
About 60 degrees, perpendicular to the inguinal crease

questions.stem: In the PENG block, which landmarks should be clear after sliding the probe medially?
questions.answer: Anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS), iliopubic eminence (IPE) and psoas tendon

questions.stem: In the PENG block, what does sliding distally or tilting caudally show?
In the PENG block, where should the psoas tendon sit when you return to the scanning line?
What needle length is used for the PENG block?
In the PENG block, in which direction is the in-plane needle advanced?
What volume of long-acting local anaesthetic is injected in the PENG block?
Which long-acting local anaesthetic is given as an example for the PENG block?
